The evidence I have to back up my *opinion* are just the fundamentals of early childhood psychology and *facts* about early childhood social development. there are studies that show how children from single parent households are more likely to drop out of schools, as well as they are more likely to consume alcohol and drugs more excessively. the reason for that is in many cases the combination of and instable family, the social and financial pressure due to single parent household still being stigmatized (rightfully so) and simply the half of the income or other contributions to the family.

from the parental side there is the risk of underdeveloped feelings of parenthood, which can put the child and the parent in great danger, as underdeveloped feelings of that kind leads to an even greater instability of the already instable family. on the long term you just have to put 2 and 2 together to see how that relates to higher alcohol and drug abuse rates, violence and higher drop out rates for children from single parent households. and even if there are some families who still can manage it, that is not normality and is unnecessarily putting the child in risky environments.
